1.  Install two packages `gganimate` and `gifski` then restart Rstudio. Using the `Adult Census Income` data, make an animation using `geom_point` and `transition_states`.

    ```{r}
 
    library(gganimate)
    library(gifski)
    library(dplyr)
    library(tidyverse)
    library(lubridate)
    ```

    ```{r}

    adult <- read_csv("C:/Users/student/OneDrive - Bryant University/Documents/GitHub/math421assigntments/adult_census_missing.csv")
    adult %>% ggplot(aes(x = hours.per.week,
               y = age, color = race))+
      geom_point()+
      transition_states(sex)+
      labs(title = 'sex: {closest_state}')
    ```

2.  Using the `Adult Census Income` data, make an animation using `geom_bar` and `transition_states`.

    ```{r}
    adult %>% ggplot(aes(x = sex,
               fill = marital.status))+
      geom_bar(position = 'fill')+
      transition_states(race)+
      labs(title = 'race: {closest_state}')
    ```

3.  Use the WHO's dataset at [this link](../data/WHO-COVID-19-global-data.csv). Make a top-10 bar race by months between countries on the number of deaths by Covid 19 in 2021.

    ```{r}
    covid <- read_csv("C:/Users/student/OneDrive - Bryant University/Documents/GitHub/math421assigntments/WHO-COVID-19-global-data.csv")

    covid$month <- month(covid$Date_reported)
    covid1 <- covid %>% group_by(month, Country) %>% summarise(mean = mean(Cumulative_deaths))
    covid2 <- covid1 %>% group_by(month) %>% mutate(rank=rank(-mean)) 
    covid3 <- covid2 %>% filter(rank <= 10)

    a1 <- covid3 %>% ggplot(aes(x = rank, y = mean, group = Country, fill = Country, label = Country)) + geom_col()+
        geom_text(aes(y = mean, label = Country), hjust = 1.4)+ 
        coord_flip(clip = "off", expand = FALSE) +scale_x_reverse()+
        labs(title = 'Month {closest_state}', x='', y = 'Total Number of Deaths', fill= 'Country')+
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 22),
              axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
              axis.text.y  = element_blank()) + 
        transition_states(month)+
        ease_aes("cubic-in-out")

    animate(a1, nframes = 400)
    ```

4.  Make a bar race using a dataset of your own interest. You may use the dataset that we use in class (<https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/all-states-history.csv>) but you should make a different bar racev from ones in the slides.

    ```{r}
    states <- read_csv("C:/Users/student/OneDrive - Bryant University/Documents/GitHub/math421assigntments/all-states-history.csv")


    states$week <- week(states$date)
    states1 <- states %>% group_by(week, state) %>% summarise(mean = mean(hospitalized))
    states2 <- states1 %>% group_by(week) %>% mutate(rank=rank(-mean)) 
    states3 <- states2 %>% filter(rank <= 5)

    a1 <- states3 %>% ggplot(aes(x=rank, y=mean, group=state, fill=state, label=state)) + geom_col()+
        geom_text(aes(y = mean, label = state), hjust = 1.4)+ 
        coord_flip(clip = "off", expand = FALSE) +scale_x_reverse()+
        labs(title = 'Week {closest_state}', x='', y='Total Number of hospitalizations', fill='state')+
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 22),
              axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
              axis.text.y  = element_blank()) + 
        transition_states(week)+
        ease_aes("cubic-in-out")
    ```
